title: Digital Photo Album for Events With a QR Code [2026 Guide]
description: Create a shared digital photo album for a wedding, birthday or event. Guests scan one QR code and upload photos and videos from their browser—no app download.
author: Guestcam Team
tldr: The simplest digital photo album for an event is a shared web gallery with a QR code: the host creates the album, guests scan the code and upload selected photos or videos directly from their phone browser.
coverAlt: Event guests taking photos with their smartphones

content.text: What is a digital photo album for an event?

A digital event photo album is one shared web gallery where photos and videos from many phones can be collected in the same place. Instead of chasing files through WhatsApp chats, email attachments and separate cloud folders after the event, you give everyone one QR code or guest link.

The QR code does not store the photos itself. It simply opens the gallery. A guest scans it with the phone camera, opens the album and chooses which files to share. With Guestcam, guests do not need to install an app or create an account to upload.
How to create an event photo album with a QR code in 5 steps

items: Create the event and give the album a name guests will recognise.
Open the guest view and test it on another phone.
Download the QR code or copy the guest link.
Put the QR code on table cards, a welcome sign or the event programme; share the direct link by message too.
After the event, send the same link again so guests can add photos they did not upload during the celebration.

content.text: QR photo album vs WhatsApp vs a shared folder

rows: One destination for all files; opens in a browser
Photos mix with conversation and can be harder to organise later
Works well for a small group already using the service
Accounts and permissions can add steps for some guests
Large attachments and many separate messages

content.text: A useful combination is to use WhatsApp or email for the reminder, and the QR album as the single destination for photos and videos.
Where should you place the QR code?

items: On tables where guests can scan it comfortably while seated.
On a welcome sign with a clear instruction such as “Share your photos”.
Near a photo booth, bar or another spot where guests already have phones out.
On a screen if you use a Photo Wall or slideshow.
In the follow-up message the next day, include the direct link as well as the QR image.

content.text: Test the printed QR code at its final size and, if possible, in lighting similar to the venue. Keep clear space around the code and avoid placing it over detailed photos, busy patterns or reflective material.
Can you show the album live during the event?

Yes. A Photo Wall or slideshow can turn the shared album into part of the event by showing uploaded photos on a TV, projector or other display. Guests can see that submissions are arriving, and the QR code can stay visible on screen. If moderation is enabled, photos appear only after approval.

items: Share the QR code and link mainly with people invited to the event.
Use available access or moderation controls when you need an extra layer of control.
Make it clear that guests choose the files they upload.
After the event, download important memories and keep your own backup.

content.q: Do guests have to download an app?
content.a: No. Guests open Guestcam through a QR code or link in their phone browser.

content.q: Can every guest use the same QR code?
content.a: Yes. You can print the same code in several places; everyone reaches the same event album.

content.q: Does the QR code work without internet?
content.a: A phone may recognise the code offline, but the gallery and file uploads require an internet connection.

content.q: What events can use a shared QR photo album?
content.a: Weddings, birthdays, christenings, graduations, baby showers, anniversaries, parties and corporate events are all common examples.

content.q: Can uploaded photos be shown live?
content.a: Yes. With Photo Wall or slideshow, the shared album can be displayed on a screen during the event.
